Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR replaces the Usage page with native session analytics, charts, custom ranges, provider allowances and CSV exports. **Example:** Inspect usage for October 21–27, 2026. - **Before:** The page provides aggregate totals, daily costs and provider plans. - **After:** Users can inspect contributing agents, models and sessions, expand session details and export the selected range. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Useful owner-directed feature, but three source-confirmed defects block correctness and historical captures do not establish the current behavior. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 3 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Windows users cannot identify the sessions, agents and models driving usage or inspect a custom reporting range. **Reason:** The collaborator-authored direction supplies useful native analysis while explicitly leaving deeper analytics to the web page. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 3 items remain** Keep open: this collaborator-authored feature adds useful analysis absent from main, but three correctness defects need repair before merge. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e` ## Before merge - [ ] **Recheck the originating Gateway before writing the selected CSV file (P2)** - Start an export on Gateway A, leave the Save picker pending, then replace the client with Gateway B, for example through the existing local connection command. Gateway replacement resets state inside the same controller, so this identity check still passes and FileIO.WriteTextAsync writes A's report. UsageExportWorkflow checks the Gateway only after save returns, which merely suppresses the notification. Carry the originating connection guard into the save callback and check it after the picker returns, immediately before writing. - [ ] **Withhold session percentages when the range report is incomplete (P2)** - A report can have partial or stale cache status while its numeric totals and one completed session have no lower-bound flag. With $5 currently aggregated and a completed $5 session, this code displays an exact 100% share even though other sessions remain uncomputed. The hero and contributor policies already reject this state, but session details check only per-total flags and missing prices. Apply the same report/cache completeness requirement before rendering the percentage. - [ ] **Use the expiry-aware allowance policy for provider warning badges (P2)** - A provider window reporting 90% with ResetAt already passed still satisfies NearLimit, so the rendered provider row continues showing Near limit and its attention action. The source's expiry callback invalidates AttentionCount but retains the display snapshot, and the row ignores UsageProviderAttention.Select, which already rejects expired windows and provider errors. Reuse that validity policy for the badge while retaining historical allowance text as appropriate. ## Findings - [P2] Recheck the originating Gateway before writing the selected CSV file — `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs:139-141` - [P2] Withhold session percentages when the range report is incomplete — `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/Usage/UsageSessionsSection.cs:35-38` - [P2] Use the expiry-aware allowance policy for provider warning badges — `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Presentation/Usage/UsageInsights.cs:9-10` ### Tests - Low-value test `tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/Usage/UsageSessionDetailAndExportTests.cs`: Remove the helper-only SummaryRow test, which restates null coalescing, and protect fallback behavior through the rendered detail surface instead. - Missing end-to-end proof: Current-candidate visible Usage behavior, real-Gateway compatibility and native Save-picker completion remain unproved; the new fixes also need failing-before/passing-after regressions.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Usage controller sends authenticated operator reads to the Gateway, projects reported metadata into Reactor views, and delegates chat navigation, browser launch and CSV saving to existing Windows owners. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Usage controls] --> B[Usage controller] B --> C[Operator Gateway client] C --> D[Gateway usage methods] D --> E[Typed usage projections] E --> F[Native charts and sessions] B --> G[CSV save and navigation] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the controller/projection split, fence exports immediately before file writing, and reuse the existing completeness and allowance-validity policies. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? The three failing paths follow directly from current source and existing input models; no target code, build or tests were executed during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The native analysis feature has clear value, and its existing owners can handle the remaining fixes without additional services or configuration. Full review comments: - [P2] Recheck the originating Gateway before writing the selected CSV file — `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs:139-141` Start an export on Gateway A, leave the Save picker pending, then replace the client with Gateway B, for example through the existing local connection command. Gateway replacement resets state inside the same controller, so this identity check still passes and FileIO.WriteTextAsync writes A's report. UsageExportWorkflow checks the Gateway only after save returns, which merely suppresses the notification. Carry the originating connection guard into the save callback and check it after the picker returns, immediately before writing. Confidence: 0.96 - [P2] Withhold session percentages when the range report is incomplete — `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/Usage/UsageSessionsSection.cs:35-38` A report can have partial or stale cache status while its numeric totals and one completed session have no lower-bound flag. With $5 currently aggregated and a completed $5 session, this code displays an exact 100% share even though other sessions remain uncomputed. The hero and contributor policies already reject this state, but session details check only per-total flags and missing prices. Apply the same report/cache completeness requirement before rendering the percentage. Confidence: 0.97 - [P2] Use the expiry-aware allowance policy for provider warning badges — `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Presentation/Usage/UsageInsights.cs:9-10` A provider window reporting 90% with ResetAt already passed still satisfies NearLimit, so the rendered provider row continues showing Near limit and its attention action. The source's expiry callback invalidates AttentionCount but retains the display snapshot, and the row ignores UsageProviderAttention.Select, which already rejects expired windows and provider errors. Reuse that validity policy for the badge while retaining historical allowance text as appropriate. Confidence: 0.96 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.94 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [1c223f14f6b6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/1c223f14f6b66cf0928eeb8686f34208b5ea4d51). ### Provenance checked - `Usage period selection and reconnect recovery` keeps the original intent (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/508: Prevent disconnected loads from remaining blank and recover when the Gateway reconnects; the replacement retains lifecycle subscriptions and response fencing.) - `Older-Gateway aggregate fallback` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (d4284d43fb6a8d23cf4f011adcc132d32a0d4df1: The former policy accepted an initial mismatched cost period to avoid indefinite loading on older Gateways; the current description explicitly replaces that compatibility path with an unsupported/update state.) - `Operator facade and page ownership` keeps the original intent (990a7f4a5f741ca00988abf07d225ff8e3a986fe: Expose operator reads without giving pages connection lifecycle control; the new page continues using the manager-owned client.) - `Reactor dependency` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (a4dd026cc5f85a444a0fcd05eef5b86282dbda8c: Preview.16 carried the chat recycled-anchor workaround; this PR deliberately adopts the published preview.17 pair and verified acquisition path for the new page.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - ./scripts/Initialize-ReactorPackages.ps1 - ./scripts/test-reactor-packages.ps1 - ./build.ps1 - dotnet build ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj - dotnet build ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj What I checked: - **Scope and owner direction:** The full PR body explicitly scopes the compact native feature, accepts removal of the old usage.cost fallback for unsupported Gateways, and identifies current-candidate runtime validation as incomplete; the author is a collaborator. ([28b94333b17c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e)) - **Verified introduced change:** The pinned main-to-head diff contains the Usage replacement and supporting changes; main still uses the aggregate-only page. ([`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs), [28b94333b17c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e)) - **Export write boundary:** After the native picker returns, SaveCsvAsync checks page-controller identity but not the originating Gateway; the workflow checks Gateway identity only after this callback has written the file. ([`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs:140`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/UsagePage.xaml.cs#L140), [28b94333b17c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e)) - **Inconsistent completeness policies:** Session-detail percentages omit report/cache incompleteness checks that HeroContributors and ContributorSharesKnown already apply. ([`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/Usage/UsageSessionsSection.cs:35`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Pages/Usage/UsageSessionsSection.cs#L35), [28b94333b17c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e)) - **Competing allowance predicates:** Provider rows use NearLimit, which checks only the percentage, while UsageProviderAttention.Select rejects expired windows and provider errors. ([`src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Presentation/Usage/UsageInsights.cs:9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e/src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Presentation/Usage/UsageInsights.cs#L9), [28b94333b17c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e)) - **Exact-head CI and inspection limit:** Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/42713621730 completed with failures in Tray UI tests and mock-Gateway scenarios; build, core/tray, packaging, stable-profile compatibility and Axe steps passed. Failure annotations provide only exit codes, and log retrieval was blocked at productionresultssa1.blob.core.windows.net, so neither failure is attributed to the diff. ([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [28b94333b17c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/28b94333b17cf358f6cd9e6a0cf6ddd5ba3a4e5e)) Likely related people: - **Ranjesh Jaganathan:** Raw commit 990a7f4a5f741ca00988abf07d225ff8e3a986fe adds src/OpenClaw.Shared/IOperatorGatewayClient.cs:10 relative to its recorded parents. This identifies author metadata, not feature responsibility or a PR merger. (role: source-line author; confidence: high; commits: [990a7f4a5f74](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/990a7f4a5f741ca00988abf07d225ff8e3a986fe); files: `src/OpenClaw.Shared/IOperatorGatewayClient.cs`) - **Scott Hanselman:** Raw commit 0b31e210a42106cae755e6e18f8259afeac6c527 adds src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs:1645 relative to its recorded parents. This identifies author metadata, not feature responsibility or a PR merger. (role: source-line author; confidence: medium; commits: [0b31e210a421](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/commit/0b31e210a42106cae755e6e18f8259afeac6c527); files: `src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs`) ### Preflight source Source unknown. Source comparison at the observed PR snapshot only. Completion is self-reported; body, policy, tests, execution, and report bytes are not verified. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production and test delta** | Production +5,762/-830 lines; tests and fixtures +7,236/-96 lines | The feature includes substantial protocol, lifecycle, export and native-rendering coverage, making a focused consistency repair preferable to another architectural rewrite. | ### Labels Label changes: - add `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`: Overall readiness is 🧂 unranked krab; proof is 🧂 unranked krab and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - remove `rating: 🦪 silver shellfish`: Current PR rating is `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`, so this older rating label is no longer current. Label justifications: - `P2`: This is a useful analytics improvement with bounded export and presentation defects, rather than an urgent core-runtime outage. - `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`: An export can retain the previous Gateway's session data through a client replacement and still write it. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: Gateways without compatible sessions.usage lose the page's previous aggregate fallback; this tradeoff is explicitly accepted in the collaborator-authored description. - `rating: 🧂 unranked krab`: Overall readiness is 🧂 unranked krab; proof is 🧂 unranked krab and patch quality is 🦪 silver shellfish. - `status: ⏳ waiting on author`: ClawSweeper has contributor-facing work open and is waiting for author action. ### Rating scale 6/6 🦀 challenger crab · 5/6 🦞 diamond lobster · 4/6 🐚 platinum hermit · 3/6 🦐 gold shrimp · 2/6 🦪 silver shellfish · 1/6 🧂 unranked krab. Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality; ✨ marks media proof (a screenshot, video, or linked artifact) that directly shows the changed behavior. ### Workflow ClawSweeper edits this one comment on every review. Comment `@clawsweeper re-review` for a fresh review only. Repair and merge execution lanes are retired. ### History

## Current-head validation and UI proof

Candidate: `86d8597214a32d78ee7be518aeaf5a5876817ba4`, including a merge of `main` at `48cb8a18`. The six locale conflicts were resolved by keeping both sets of resource additions. No Usage implementation code changed in that merge.

**Still blocked, not CI-green.** [Build and Test, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/40581344544) ran after the conflict resolution. Core/CLI, fast validation, proof-pool contracts and release metadata passed. The stock Reactor package still reports the seven analyzer errors. The two analyzer fixes, microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor#1427 and microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor#1428, are now merged, but a compatible published package containing them has not been verified.

Native proof below uses a temporary, local-only `0.1.0-preview.12-local.2` package containing those two analyzer fixes. It does not establish a successful build from the committed dependency graph. Neither the local feed nor its version pins are committed.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `.\build.ps1` with local analyzer-only Reactor package | Passed |
| Full Shared tests | 4,671 passed, 3 failed, 25 skipped |
| Full Tray tests | 4,615 passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped |
| Focused Shared Usage plus MXC command-runner recheck | 99 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| Focused Tray Usage/localization plus the three chat failure owners | 322 passed, 0 failed/skipped |
| Real-process x64 accessibility plus startup tests | 24 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped. The Usage page case passed. The failure is two unnamed expanders on SandboxPage, not Usage. |

The full-run failures are retained, not replaced by the focused passes. Shared's three failures were command-runner deadlines/output under load. Tray had the four previously observed ARM64 build-prerequisite failures and three chat/concurrency/HTTP-timeout failures. No Usage test failed. The PR body lists the exact commands and limitations.

An independent rubber-duck review checked the final fix round at `b3c8dc4d`, found no new blocking source finding, and ran 116 Tray Usage tests and 76 Shared Usage/Sessions tests. That is advisory source evidence. Native execution subsequently found the runtime failure below.

### New blocking native failure

Switching the fixture through populated, empty, partial and legacy states, with Settings Connection -> Usage navigation between modes, produced:

```text
Render error: InvalidCastException:
Unable to cast object of type 'Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.Border'
to type 'Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.InfoBar'.
```

The stack enters Reactor's `V1HandlerAdapter.Update` from `ChildReconciler.ReconcileKeyed`. The Usage sections have stable keys and exit transitions. A separate local Reactor investigation is reducing this; no animation removal, analyzer suppression, or other Windows-side workaround has been added. **Legacy transition proof fails.** This screenshot is failure evidence, not a passed state.

![Legacy transition fails with a Reactor keyed-child render error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34f42df0-1522-42ed-b6b5-21179c22ab9e)

### Current-source captures

These are real native app-window captures of synthetic fixture data, not a real Gateway/provider account. The profile, Gateway and MCP endpoint were isolated. Executable and managed-assembly hashes, source identity, fixture receipts and TRX files were retained locally. High contrast was enabled with approval and restored to the original None setting with approval.

<details>
<summary>Populated report and chart text equivalent</summary>

![Populated native Usage reporting range and totals](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e082f3b-a0e9-45b6-b3c9-6ee2138febfe)

![Thirty-day chart with its expanded native text table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34797cf4-4e7c-4257-bee9-a7862bbc685a)

</details>

<details>
<summary>High contrast and filtered conversation</summary>

![Native Usage header using Windows Night sky high contrast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10aca5cd-c4fc-4b30-841e-ee66c7ee0d91)

![Conversation search narrows synthetic logs from 24 to 6 messages](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66f45b59-0db7-4008-9cab-1f877ee14393)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Empty and partial reports</summary>

![Empty report shows zero totals and the native empty state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae1c59e0-0aca-4d9b-a996-6bf4fc0c5521)

![Partial report shows lower-bound totals and partial/cache banners](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79465e4f-d074-4947-9579-11fd50055215)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Released-Gateway fallback, dark theme and disconnected state</summary>

![Dark-theme basic view for the released Gateway schema with unsupported filters hidden](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78e0eaa0-1079-4a49-9a72-30c13c4ccc49)

![Disconnected Usage page with disabled refresh/export and Open Connection action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a97af9f-8d74-4545-b2a2-9787b31fac41)

</details>

The disconnected banner's own **Open Connection** button was invoked and the native `ConnectionPageMarker` appeared. Conversation search was exercised through the native field and showed **6 of 24 messages** for `Checking`. The daily chart's text table was expanded and exposed dates, token counts and costs.

Remaining gaps: failing legacy transition; current-source real-Gateway execution; full native proof-pool completion; populated Usage Axe scan; full session-summary/timeline/context, export-picker and keyboard coverage. These captures do not complete the entire `windows-winui-interactive` pool.

## Corrected Reactor runtime: consumer retest

Windows source remains **`86d8597214a32d78ee7be518aeaf5a5876817ba4`**. No Windows animation workaround or implementation change was made. This retest used a temporary, unpublished **`0.1.0-preview.12-local.4`** package with the two analyzer fixes, the keyed-exit correction and its prerequisite exit bookkeeping/attached-property post-pass. It is not a stock-package or green-CI result.

| Required command | Latest local result |
|---|---|
| `.\build.ps1` | Passed on native ARM64 with the neutral local.4 package |
| `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore --logger 'trx;LogFileName=shared.trx' --results-directory $out` | 4,674 passed, 0 failed, 25 skipped |
| `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore --logger 'trx;LogFileName=tray.trx' --results-directory $out` | 4,618 passed, 4 failed, 0 skipped |

`$out` was the absolute path to `artifacts\usage-proof\86d85972-local4`, with `OPENCLAW_REPO_ROOT` set to this worktree. The four remaining failures are `BuildPrerequisiteTests.CheckOnly_UsesTheAppLocalRuntimeResolver`, previously reproduced on the unchanged ARM64 baseline. No Usage test failed. Earlier failures and the failed x64-only local.3 package attempt remain retained; the newer results do not erase them.

### Original cast failure no longer occurs in the replay

With the exact neutral DLL payloads deployed, computer-use observed:

1. Populated: 1.3M tokens, $4.51, 11 sessions.
2. Empty: zero totals and the empty state.
3. Partial: lower-bound totals and partial/cache banners.
4. Legacy: `UsageLegacyBanner` and the session-less cost view remained rendered, without the prior `Border` to `InfoBar` cast error. This synthetic legacy response had no daily values in the selected range; it does not prove populated legacy cost accuracy.
5. Released after reconnect: 1.3M tokens, $4.51, 11 sessions, `UsageBasicBanner`, and unsupported query/day/hour filters absent.

Before-correction failure: [original native failure capture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34f42df0-1522-42ed-b6b5-21179c22ab9e).

![The original legacy transition stays rendered with the local Reactor correction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65f641e4-c0b5-407b-b0e6-cca59e07a147)

**Visual acceptance is still incomplete.** High contrast was already active on the shared desktop during this round, with client-area animations enabled. This round did not change desktop settings. In the released/basic view, native data is present but the plotted daily bars are not visible in the capture below. The cause is not yet attributed. A same-consumer local.2 runtime comparison failed during startup, so it is not valid A/B evidence. A bounded native probe is investigating geometry, brush and animation state.

![Remaining visual issue: released-mode daily plot has data but no visible bars under the existing high-contrast desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1336921a-52bc-4a79-a678-cc8e9aa3f101)

### Dependency proof and boundaries

- The child reproduced three exact preview.12 cast failures before the keyed correction. Its native tests cover leading, trailing, middle and same-key Grid replacements, including live identity/placement after exits.
- The neutral packaged bytes passed **9 transition fixtures, 0 failures** on the native ARM64 Reactor host, including **4 keyed fixtures / 15 assertions**.
- The consumer's three deployed DLL hashes exactly matched the package payloads before launch.
- The core package SHA256 is `5E12CC8E0D6AEA8442E20A64AFE29076299C6235380F25DFD98CC9DB6B0694AE`; Advanced is `C4BB5C86C46E6DE89150513351138D42DA209601DFF520748ED6C6DCF17E9B36`.
- The authoritative Reactor correction and preview.12 backport remain local and uncommitted. No new Reactor PR or remote package publication is claimed.
- The temporary consumer feed and pins have been removed. Windows' working tree is clean, and the task-owned fixture was stopped.

**CI remains blocked** on the committed stock package. A compatible published Reactor release and a reviewed consumer dependency update are still needed. This is not complete `windows-winui-interactive` or real-Gateway proof; the chart issue and other declared proof gaps remain open.

Current Windows candidate: `f285853d2b6134e000d56ca6a8cca6808e8054a3`. These are **current-source native ARM64 app captures**, using the isolated synthetic Gateway fixture and architecture-neutral Reactor `0.1.0-preview.12-local.4`. They are not stock-package CI or real-Gateway proof.

The local package contains the two analyzer fixes plus the keyed-exit correction now proposed in [microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor#1429](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/pull/1429). No temporary package feed/pins or Windows-side animation workaround is published.

The replay survived populated -> empty -> partial -> legacy -> released, including Connection -> Usage remounts. The former Border-to-InfoBar crash did not recur. Populated totals were 1.3M tokens, $4.51 and 11 sessions; the expanded seven-day text table agreed with chart accessibility names. Partial mode showed lower-bound totals and partial/cache banners. Released-schema mode hid unsupported query controls and rendered nonzero bars. The legacy fixture returned no daily rows, so that capture proves transition/fallback rendering, not populated legacy-cost accuracy. After shutting down only the owned fixture transport, Usage disabled Refresh/Export and its Open Connection action opened Connection settings.

`f285853d` also corrects the chart's high-contrast data-token choice: `UsagePalette1Brush`, rather than the native button-fill token that can match the plot background. Two mounted native regression cases (interactive and basic charts) failed at the intended color assertion before the fix and passed afterward, with nonzero layout and an independent native button-fill control. Those cases supply controlled high-contrast resource input without changing the desktop theme. **The captures below are normal Light theme, not current-head whole-page high-contrast proof.**

Earlier proof comments describe older source/runtime combinations and retain their original failures. The failed local.3 x64-only package build and failed local.2 comparison startup are not successful consumer A/B evidence. Current stock CI remains blocked by seven upstream analyzer false positives; the local-package results do not make CI green. Complete interactive/real-Gateway proof pools, populated Usage Axe coverage, complete session-detail/export-picker/keyboard acceptance and production-packaged acceptance remain unverified.

Seven captures follow in replay order: released/basic with visible bars; populated with expanded text table; empty with independent provider usage; partial; legacy without the former render error; disconnected; Open Connection destination.

![Current candidate in normal Light theme, released-schema basic view with visible daily bars](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cd3f9e2-a9e7-4e25-a18d-e2c84f620968)

![Current candidate, populated daily chart and expanded matching text table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3af44a7-6ed3-4dd9-98fe-6bfdac33cf3c)

![Current candidate, empty report while provider-plan usage remains separate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9deb70ab-51ff-47e8-8c5e-51529659131a)

### Socket protects your app from malicious dependencies lurking in your open source supply chain.

Open source code makes up 90% of most codebases. It is critical to manage it effectively to reduce your security risk.

## Detect and block open source supply chain attacks

Security teams depend on Socket to prevent malicious open source dependencies from infiltrating their apps.

Socket dramatically improves your open source security posture by _detecting and blocking the attacks you don't expect_ – malware, install scripts, hidden code, typo-squatting, and more – which aren't caught by traditional vulnerability scanners.

- **Block malware** – Block emerging malware threats

- **Block typo-squatting** – Block malicious packages that differ in name by only a few characters, and recommend the correct package

- **Detect hidden code** – Detect obfuscated, minified, or hidden code

- **Detect privileged API usage** – Report when a dependency update introduces new risky API usage – filesystem, network, child_process, eval()

- **Detect suspicious updates** – Sudden inclusion of privileged APIs in patch or minor releases

Socket currently [supports 80+ detections](https://socket.dev/alerts) in 5 categories: supply chain risk, quality, maintenance, known vulnerabilities, and license problems.

## Take charge of your dependency health

Socket improves security outcomes and reduces work for security teams by **surfacing actionable security information directly inline in GitHub** so developers are empowered to make better decisions.

- **Five minute deployment** – The easiest security product you'll ever deploy in your organization. Just install a GitHub app and you're done.

- **Provide security feedback directly on PRs** – Empower developers to solve security issues before they're deployed into production.

- **Automated security** – Spend security team resources auditing the highest-impact dependencies, instead of all or nothing.

## Socket detects what vulnerability scanners can’t

It's no longer sufficient to scan for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and stop there. And yet, that's what the leading "supply chain security" products do, leaving you vulnerable.

It can take weeks or months for a CVE to be discovered, reported, and detected by tools. But in today's culture of fast development, a malicious dependency can be updated, merged, and running in production in days or even sometimes hours.

Defenders need a new approach to address emerging threats from malicious dependencies:

- **Maintainer intentionally added malware** – Rogue maintainer sabotaged his own open source package with 100M downloads/month, affecting companies such as Amazon AWS

- **Package hijacked and poisoned w/ cryptominers and password-stealing malware** – Deliberate malware introduced into multiple packages with 30M downloads/month each

- **Package hijacked to add backdoor targeting a specific organization** – Obfuscated malware added to a dependency which targeted a single company, went undetected for over a week, and made it into their production build

- **NPM package manager allowed anyone to publish new versions of any package** – Attackers could publish new versions of any NPM package without authorization _for multiple years_

Using third-party dependencies without proper vetting leaves you open to hacking, breaches, and assorted security misfortune.
